bug_description.normalized: The saved PoC is the exact UART line `coap put :F:0:0:C:0:F:F:.\n`. In the staged vulnerable checkout at `21ad4f5da3ae085cd08997c52bd3fd053501a125`, `ot::Cli::Uart::ReceiveTask` copies the first 25 bytes into `mRxBuffer`; the trailing newline NUL-terminates the command, `ProcessLine` tokenizes it into `coap`, `put`, and `:F:0:0:C:0:F:F:.`, and the CoAP `put` handler passes that address string into `otIp6AddressFromString` for stack `coapDestinationIp`. Inside `ot::Ip6::Address::FromString`, the leading `:` sets `colonp = mFields.m8 - 1`, the seven colon-terminated hex groups write 14 bytes so `dst = mFields.m8 + 13`, and the final `.` executes `endp -= kIp4AddressSize`, moving `endp` back to `mFields.m8 + 11` after `dst` has already advanced past it. Because the staged vulnerable code lacks the fix's added `VerifyOrExit(dst <= endp, error = OT_ERROR_PARSE)` before `break`, it falls straight into `while (colonp && dst > colonp)` and the loop-body store `*endp-- = *dst--;` at line 333 eventually writes `mFields.m8[-1]`, one byte before the 16-byte `coapDestinationIp` stack object, producing the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow.

source.description: This is the first staged project statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled input: each non-newline UART byte is appended into `mRxBuffer`, building the CLI command string later terminated and parsed.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` bytes are the ASCII sequence `coap put :F:0:0:C:0:F:F:.\n`. `ReceiveTask` executes this append for the first 25 bytes, then the trailing newline takes the line-147/150 command-finalization path, writes the terminating NUL, and invokes `ProcessCommand`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: After CLI tokenization and both command-dispatch steps, `argv[1]` is the exact address token `:F:0:0:C:0:F:F:.`; `ProcessRequest` passes it directly into `Address::FromString`, where it drives the later `colonp`, `dst`, and `endp` state.

root_cause.description: When the final `.` selects embedded-IPv4 mode after 14 IPv6 bytes have already been written, this subtracts four bytes from `endp`, moving it to `mFields.m8 + 11` while `dst` is already `mFields.m8 + 13`. The fixing patch inserts `VerifyOrExit(dst <= endp, error = OT_ERROR_PARSE)` here; in the staged vulnerable source execution falls straight to the compaction loop with `dst > endp`.

sink.description: This compaction-loop store is the exact ASan crash site in the staged source. After enough iterations it writes to `mFields.m8[-1]`, underflowing the 16-byte stack `coapDestinationIp` object by one byte.

parser_admitted.description: After the newline path has NUL-terminated the buffered 25-byte command, `ProcessCommand` forwards that completed CLI line to the interpreter.

fine_trace.note: Source. For each non-newline byte of the saved witness, this append copies the UART byte into `mRxBuffer`. Across the first 25 bytes, it materializes `mRxBuffer = "coap put :F:0:0:C:0:F:F:."` and advances `mRxLength` to 25.
When the trailing `\n` reaches the newline case, the accumulated bytes are NUL-terminated and `ProcessCommand` executes the completed CLI line.
The interpreter tokenizes the NUL-terminated line in place. For this witness it yields `argc = 3`, `argv[0] = "coap"`, `argv[1] = "put"`, and `argv[2] = ":F:0:0:C:0:F:F:."`.

With `cmd = "coap"`, the built-in command table selects `ProcessCoap` and shifts the token vector by one, so the CoAP handler receives `argc = 2`, `argv[0] = "put"`, and `argv[1] = ":F:0:0:C:0:F:F:."`.
In the CoAP subcommand table, `argv[0] == "put"` selects `ProcessRequest`. The call preserves `argc = 2` and forwards the address token in `argv[1]` unchanged.
ProcessRequest passes the exact address token `:F:0:0:C:0:F:F:.` into `otIp6AddressFromString` to fill local 16-byte stack `coapDestinationIp`, the object ASan later reports at `[176, 192)`.

fine_trace.code:
VerifyOrExit(colonp == NULL || first, error = OT_ERROR_PARSE);
colonp = dst;
fine_trace.note: The first address character is `':'` and `count == 0`, so the parser records `colonp = dst`. Because `dst` was decremented once at line 276 before parsing, `colonp` becomes `mFields.m8 - 1`, one byte before the destination buffer.

For the seven colon-terminated hex groups in `F:0:0:C:0:F:F:`, this guarded write sequence executes seven times. The present bound check `dst + 2 <= endp` succeeds on each iteration while `endp` is still `mFields.m8 + 15`, so 14 bytes are written to `mFields.m8[0..13]` and `dst` finishes at `mFields.m8 + 13`.

Root cause. The final `.` takes the embedded-IPv4 branch and reserves four tail bytes by moving `endp` from `mFields.m8 + 15` to `mFields.m8 + 11`, but `dst` is already `mFields.m8 + 13`. The staged vulnerable source then `break`s without the fix's added `VerifyOrExit(dst <= endp, error = OT_ERROR_PARSE)`.

With `colonp = mFields.m8 - 1`, `dst = mFields.m8 + 13`, and `endp = mFields.m8 + 11`, this compaction-loop condition is true. Execution therefore enters backward copying even though the destination pointer already starts two bytes behind the source pointer.

Sink. Each iteration copies one byte and decrements both pointers. After 12 in-bounds copies fill `mFields.m8[11]` down through `mFields.m8[0]`, the next execution writes to `mFields.m8[-1]`, one byte before `coapDestinationIp`, matching ASan's `WRITE of size 1` at `src/core/net/ip6_address.cpp:333`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: ASan reports `src/core/net/ip6_address.cpp:333`, which is the exact `*endp-- = *dst--;` store used as the sink in the staged checkout.

format.contract: The saved witness is the exact ASCII byte sequence `coap put :F:0:0:C:0:F:F:.\n`. `ReceiveTask` must append the first 25 bytes into `mRxBuffer` via line 182, then the trailing `\n` must take the lines-147/150 command-finalization path so `ParseCmd` yields `argv[0] = "coap"`, `argv[1] = "put"`, and `argv[2] = ":F:0:0:C:0:F:F:."`; that address string must reach `Address::FromString` and hit `'.'` after seven colon-terminated 16-bit groups.
